title: Use permitted restricted notes and files
summary: Use only authorised content and review its additional read-only viewers.

sections.title: Save restricted notes and review additional read-only viewers
paragraphs: The resource must already be saved, and you must have permission to edit its restricted content. Viewing a restricted Help article does not by itself grant access to every resource’s private material.
steps: Open Manage My Resources and Edit on the exact saved Place or standard Offering that you may edit.
Open Restricted and review Restricted notes and files. If the panel cannot load or permission is denied, stop and request review of the exact resource assignment.
Enter or update only the Restricted notes you are authorised to share with the resource’s permitted viewers.
Review Additional read-only viewers and choose only the intended eligible accounts. Resource editors already have access; selecting All adds currently eligible accounts as explicit read-only viewers.
Select Save Restricted Content and wait for Restricted content saved. Reopen the permitted panel to check the notes and viewer selection.
notes: Additional read-only viewers do not gain resource editing rights. These notes are separate from My Map personal notes and Guide history.
Save Restricted Content is its own saved action; Save Place or Save Offering is not a substitute for saving the notes/viewer selection.
Review the sharing scope before choosing All. Do not assume it includes every platform account or grants access to future accounts.
Keep secrets, credentials and unnecessary personal information out of operating notes. Do not paste restricted text or attachments into the Guide.
If saving fails, retain the error without copying sensitive note contents into a report and check the current permission before retrying.

sections.title: Upload or remove an authorised private resource file
paragraphs: Use the exact resource’s permitted Restricted panel and only material approved for its authorised viewers. Upload and file removal are separate saved actions.
steps: Open the saved resource’s Restricted → Private files panel and review its permitted viewer scope.
Select Upload and choose a supported PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC file of no more than 10 MB.
Wait for Private file uploaded and check the resulting file list or permitted preview. An upload error is not confirmation that the file was stored.

To remove a file, check the exact filename and select its Delete private file control only when removal is intended. This starts removal immediately; wait for Private file removed and verify the updated list.
notes: Save Restricted Content submits notes and viewer selection. Upload and Delete private file do not wait for that button, and closing the editor does not undo a completed file action.
File previews require a server permission check. A resource link or knowledge that a file exists does not grant permission to retrieve it.
If a file is too large or unsupported, prepare a permitted format/size rather than uploading it through another public field. Check the failure message if preview or upload fails.
No file-recovery control is promised by these steps. Keep approved originals in the authorised operational system when needed.
Do not share private file links, restricted screenshots or attachment contents in the Guide or public help.

sections.title: Keep restricted notes and files within permitted access
paragraphs: Save the resource before adding restricted notes and files. In its permitted restricted-content editor, review Restricted notes and Additional read-only viewers, then save. File upload is a separate action; inspect the resulting notice and file list.
notes: Resource editors already have access. Explicit read-only viewers do not gain editing rights. Guests, basic users and unauthorised accounts cannot view the restricted content.
The editor accepts PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC files up to 10 MB each. Only upload material you are authorised to share with the permitted viewers.
These are resource-operating notes, not My Map personal notes or Guide history.
